newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast products mixed as NYMEX fluctuates.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast products mixed as NYMEX fluctuates.

text.p: U.S. West Coast bulk product prices were mixed Wednesday as buyers and sellers tracked a up-and-down NYMEX market rattled by news Russian President Boris Yeltsin will remain in hospital this week.
The president is continuing to recover from a serious case of pneumonia, which follows heart surgery late last year.
Russian is one of the world's largest oil producers.
"The numbers were everywhere," said a West Coast broker, referring to the swing in crude and petroleum product prices.
Fundamentally, supplies of gasoline in PADD 5 rose 623,000 barrels last week despite local refiners operating at 84.6 percent of capacity, a 4.9 percentage point fall on the week.
Gasoline supplies stood at 29.5 million barrels in the West Coast.
Traders also said inventories built at supply terminals because poor weather in recent weeks has lowered motorist demand.

A Salomon Brothers report released Wednesday showed the dealer tank wagon market, a gauge of prices charged at terminals, fell below spot prices during the fourth quarter as intense battles for market share in southern California forced cuts in retail prices.
The conflict of weak demand and higher NYMEX left price movements inconsistent.
CARB gasoline prices for January delivery eased a half cent to 75.50/76.50 cents a gallon in Los Angeles. Conventional gasoline firmed 0.50 to 74.50/75.50 cents a gallon.
